newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAILY NEWS
Labour Minister Mahinda Rajapakse to hold talks with trade unions at Shell Gas Lanka Ltd in bid to get them to end six-day strike, which has caused severe gas shortage in country.

Fomer Maldivian Prime Minister Ahmed Zaki dies in Singapore at the age of 65. At time of death he was serving as Maldives' permanent representative to the United Nations and high commissioner in the United Kingdom.
THE ISLAND
Six major industrial firms which rely on industrial gases face closure if a six-day labour strike at Shell Gas Lanka, Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, continues.
Davindra Mendis, opposition United National Party provincial council member and son of leading UNP politician Wijayapala Mendis, commits suicide, coroner's report says.
DIVAINA
Policemen take up position at auspicious time in newly constructed bunkers in northern areas recently captured from separatist Tamil rebels.
Security forces uncover 69 hand grenades hidden in a toilet in northern Jaffna peninsula.
LANKADEEPA
Angry villagers in northwestern province burn bus which ran over school children, wounding nine of them.
DINAMINA
Coroner gives suicide verdict in the death of Davindra Mendis, opposition United National Party povincial council member and son of leading UNP politician Wijayapala Mendis.
-- Colombo newsroom 941-434319
VEERAKESARI
Jaffna students demonstrate in front of their schools in protest of alleged rape of schoolgirl by security forces.
Security forces uncover 144 grenades in two roundups in the Jaffna peninsula.
THINAKARAN
Tamil group in northern frontline town of Vavuniya begin fast to urge government to find alternative housing for refugees who are now housed in area schools.
